# The dock

**Complexity:** 7

## Goal

Showing one terminal must not require loading the 13,000-line Terminals panel. Two features and a loose plan restructured the same dock, with the later one superseding two of three defects in the earliers prerequisite. Landing order is stated in Dependencies: containment, three tabs, viewport extraction, then the dock as its own document. At HEAD the dock still has two tabs, so none of this has landed.

## Dependencies & sequencing (2026-09-04, Board Collapse 08)

Two features and one loose plan restructured the same dock, and the later feature superseded two of
three defects in the earlier one's prerequisite. **At HEAD `shell.html` still has two dock tabs,
Agent and Kanban, so none of this has landed.** Land in this order.

1. **A dock frame does not know it is a dock** — inherited pane-scoped settings, the mode class
   applied after first paint, and a dock document posting `switchPanel` to the shell. Its defects 1
   and 2 are partly superseded by step 4, but its defect 3 and the shell-side origin checks stand,
   and step 2 depends on it.
2. **The agent dock becomes three tabs — Agent, CLI, Fleet** — and drops the Kanban pane. *The Agent
   Dock Opens Below The Top-Right Cluster* has been folded in and deleted: its collision analysis
   was written against the two-tab strip this step replaces, so it must be **re-derived against
   three tabs**.
3. **Extract the terminal viewport into a shared module** — about 1,700 lines out of the
   13,000-line Terminals panel, cited by line range. Every smaller `terminals.js` plan on the board
   lands **before** this, and the extraction re-cites its ranges at coding time; its own section map
   is already recorded as stale.
4. **The dock becomes its own document** — one `/dock` page, three tabs, one iframe. Requires
   steps 2 and 3.
